--- before/rules/pkg_sandbox.py
+++ tried/rules/pkg_sandbox.py
@@ -0,0 +1,856 @@
+#!/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.13 -I
+"""Runs a pinned Python package's code, and nothing else, in a throwaway sandbox (T-0275, Urgent #77 answer A).
+
+    rules/pkg_sandbox.py import-test <name>              host import test of a pinned pure wheel (+ its requires)
+    rules/pkg_sandbox.py build <name> --platform ios     cibuildwheel --platform ios on a pinned native sdist
+
+Those two forms are the whole interface; anything else is refused. The Claude Code permission rule that lets a
+session run downloaded package code allows only these two command lines (proposal issue, T-0275).
+
+What it enforces, in order, before any package code runs:
+  1. The interpreter is 3.12+ and isolated (-I), from the shebang.
+  2. pywidget/packages/manifest.toml is read from HEAD, and the working copy must equal it: every run is of a pin
+     that is on record in git. The package must be in it exactly once, with a files.pythonhosted.org url, a
+     file name, and a 64-hex sha256; its tier must fit the verb (pure wheel for import-test, native sdist for
+     build). requires, cibuildwheel and build tools are pins too (tiers "tool" and "build"). A native pin may
+     carry cibw_env, CIBW_* settings for its build (not CIBW_PLATFORM, CIBW_BUILD or CIBW_ARCHS, which come
+     from the manifest's python and the two iOS slices); they run inside the same sandbox.
+  3. Every file is taken from ~/.cache/pywidget/packages/<file> (filled by tools/pkg_fetch.py through terms_guard,
+     never by this script; it has no network code) and its sha256 (and byte count, if pinned) must equal the pin.
+     log/pkg-fetch.jsonl at HEAD must hold a terms_guard fetch record of the pinned url with the same sha256, and
+     the copy's blake2b-256 must equal the hash in PyPI's hashed path that the record's final URL names (M2,
+     T-0311). That makes a file dropped into the cache with a hand-committed hash a deliberate, committed forgery
+     rather than an easy slip; it cannot prove PyPI origin offline, so the sandbox stays the control.
+  4. A fresh directory is made under /tmp, outside the repository. Files are copied in and unpacked there:
+     wheels member by member (absolute paths, '..', backslashes, symlinks and duplicates refused), sdists with
+     tarfile's 'data' filter.
+  5. The package code runs as a child under /usr/bin/sandbox-exec, in its own session, with a profile that
+     (C13 review, pywidget/docs/reviews/pkg-sandbox-c13-review-odalys.md):
+       - denies every outbound IP connection (localhost too), the DNS socket and every Unix socket (H1);
+       - denies file reads by default: contents, listings and xattrs only under the run directory, the Python
+         install and named system paths (Xcode too for build); stat and readlink stay open (B1);
+       - denies writes outside the run directory, except /dev/null, /dev/tty, /dev/dtracehelper and xcrun's
+         xcrun_db-* temp files (the real xcrun_db cache is read-only);
+       - denies the Keychain's Mach services and exec of /usr/bin/security (B2), and user-preference reads and
+         writes through cfprefsd (B3);
+       - denies LaunchServices, Apple Events and launchd job creation, the routes that could start a process
+         outside this profile (T-0738).
+     Its environment is built from nothing: PIP_NO_INDEX=1, PIP_CONFIG_FILE=/dev/null (so no index URL from any
+     pip.conf), no PIP_INDEX_URL, a dead proxy (http://127.0.0.1:9) in every proxy variable, HOME,
+     CFFIXED_USER_HOME and TMPDIR inside the run directory. The import-test child also runs with -S (L1).
+     The process group is killed on every way out (exit, timeout, SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGINT). Then the run's other
+     processes are found by their sandbox, not by open files: sandboxed, and allowed to write the run directory,
+     which only this run's profile allows (the profile also forbids removing the run directory itself, so the
+     test cannot be dodged). They are killed until two passes in a row find none; one that left the process group
+     counts as a survivor and fails the run (H2, T-0317). A watchdog outside the sandbox, in its own session,
+     holds a pipe from the wrapper: it is told "done" only after a complete sweep, so if the wrapper dies first
+     (SIGKILL) or its sweep did not finish, it sweeps the run the same way and logs an "orphaned" outcome (so an
+     unfinished sweep leaves two lines for the run: the wrapper's "failed" and the watchdog's "orphaned"; a wrapper
+     still alive at the watchdog's deadline gets none, R4). TERM,
+     HUP and INT are ignored once cleanup starts, so they cannot cut it short (R1, T-0739). Each run also sweeps
+     and closes any earlier run that has a "started" line, no outcome and no live wrapper (both killed).
+  6. The child's current directory is an empty run/ folder, never an unpacked archive's directory, and every
+     Python in it runs with -I.
+Every invocation, refusals and crashes included, appends one outcome line to log/pkg-sandbox.jsonl (passed,
+failed, refused, error or killed), written in a finally (an unfinished sweep adds the watchdog's "orphaned" line); a run that reaches package code first appends a
+"started" line with the wrapper's and the profile's sha256, the manifest hash and HEAD (B4). git runs with a
+clean environment, so GIT_DIR from the session cannot stand in for the repository (M1). Package output is
+untrusted: it goes to child-output.txt in the run directory, and only the structured result is printed (M3).
+Archives over UNPACK_CAP bytes are refused before unpacking (L2). The run directory is left in place for
+inspection; /tmp is cleared at reboot.
+"""
+import datetime
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import pwd
+import re
+import shutil
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tarfile
+import tempfile
+import time
+import zipfile
+
+ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__)))
+MANIFEST_REL = "pywidget/packages/manifest.toml"
+LOG_REL = "log/pkg-sandbox.jsonl"
+FETCH_REL = "log/pkg-fetch.jsonl"  # terms_guard fetch records, written by tools/pkg_fetch.py (M2)
+PYPI_HOST = "files.pythonhosted.org"
+URL_PREFIX = "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/"
+DEAD_PROXY = "http://127.0.0.1:9"
+SANDBOX_EXEC = "/usr/bin/sandbox-exec"
+IMPORT_SECONDS = 300
+BUILD_SECONDS = 4 * 3600
+UNPACK_CAP = 1 << 30  # bytes, summed over an archive's members before anything is written (L2)
+NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^A-Za-z0-9?$")
+FILE_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]*$")
+SHA_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
+MODULE_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(?:\.[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)*$")
+CIBW_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^CIBW_[A-Z0-9_]+$")
+FIXED_CIBW = {"CIBW_PLATFORM", "CIBW_BUILD", "CIBW_ARCHS"}
+USAGE = "usage: rules/pkg_sandbox.py import-test <name> | rules/pkg_sandbox.py build <name> --platform ios"
+CAUGHT = (signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIGHUP, signal.SIGINT)
+
+
+class Refused(Exception):
+    pass
+
+
+class Killed(Exception):
+    """The wrapper got SIGTERM, SIGHUP or SIGINT; the child's process group is killed and the run is logged."""
+
+
+def _on_signal(signum, frame):
+    raise Killed(signal.Signals(signum).name)
+
+
+def now():
+    return datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds")
+
+
+def canon(name):
+    return re.sub(r"[-_.]+", "-", name).lower()
+
+
+def sha256_of(path):
+    h = hashlib.sha256()
+    with open(path, "rb") as f:
+        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
+            h.update(block)
+    return h.hexdigest()
+
+
+def log(record):
+    path = os.path.join(ROOT, LOG_REL)
+    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
+    with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
+        f.write(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- arguments and the manifest
+
+def parse_args(argv):
+    if len(argv) == 2 and argv[0] == "import-test":
+        verb, name = argv
+    elif len(argv) == 4 and argv[0] == "build" and argv[2] == "--platform":
+        verb, name = argv[0], argv[1]
+        if argv[3] != "ios":
+            raise Refused(f"build supports --platform ios only, not {argv[3]!r}")
+    else:
+        raise Refused(USAGE)
+    if not NAME_RE.match(name):
+        raise Refused(f"{name!r} is not a package name")
+    return verb, name
+
+
+def git(*args):
+    """git on ROOT with an environment built from nothing, so GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE or GIT_CONFIG_* from the
+    session cannot point "HEAD" at another repository (review M1)."""
+    env = {"PATH": "/usr/bin:/bin", "HOME": pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir, "GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM": "1",
+           "LANG": "C"}
+    return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, *args], capture_output=True, timeout=30, env=env)
+
+
+def load_manifest():
+    import tomllib
+    if not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(ROOT, ".git")) and not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(ROOT, ".git")):
+        raise Refused(f"{ROOT} is not a git checkout; the manifest has to come from HEAD")
+    p = git("show", f"HEAD:{MANIFEST_REL}")
+    if p.returncode != 0:
+        raise Refused(f"{MANIFEST_REL} is not in HEAD")
+    head = p.stdout
+    c = git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
+    commit = c.stdout.decode("ascii", "replace").strip() if c.returncode == 0 else None
+    try:
+        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, MANIFEST_REL), "rb") as f:
+            work = f.read()
+    except OSError:
+        work = None
+    if work != head:
+        raise Refused(f"{MANIFEST_REL} has uncommitted changes; commit the pin first so the run is on record")
+    try:
+        data = tomllib.loads(head.decode("utf-8"))
+    except (UnicodeDecodeError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError) as e:
+        raise Refused(f"{MANIFEST_REL} does not parse: {e}")
+    if data.get("format") != 1:
+        raise Refused(f"{MANIFEST_REL} format {data.get('format')!r} is not 1")
+    return data, hashlib.sha256(head).hexdigest(), commit
+
+
+def find(data, name):
+    hits = [e for e in data.get("package", []) if isinstance(e, dict) and canon(str(e.get("name", ""))) == canon(name)]
+    if not hits:
+        raise Refused(f"{name} is not pinned in {MANIFEST_REL}")
+    if len(hits) > 1:
+        raise Refused(f"{name} is pinned {len(hits)} times in {MANIFEST_REL}")
+    return hits[0]
+
+
+def check_pin(e):
+    name = e.get("name")
+    for k in ("version", "file", "url", "sha256"):
+        if not isinstance(e.get(k), str) or not e.get(k):
+            raise Refused(f"{name} has no {k} pin (status: {e.get('status', 'none')})")
+    f, url, sha = e["file"], e["url"], e["sha256"]
+    if not FILE_RE.match(f) or f in (".", ".."):
+        raise Refused(f"{name}: file {f!r} is not a plain file name")
+    if not SHA_RE.match(sha):
+        raise Refused(f"{name}: sha256 pin {sha!r} is not 64 lowercase hex digits")
+    if not url.startswith(URL_PREFIX) or url.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] != f or "?" in url or "#" in url:
+        raise Refused(f"{name}: url must be {URL_PREFIX}.../{f}")
+    if "bytes" in e and (not isinstance(e["bytes"], int) or isinstance(e["bytes"], bool) or e["bytes"] <= 0):
+        raise Refused(f"{name}: bytes pin {e['bytes']!r} is not a positive integer")
+    return e
+
+
+def load_fetches():
+    """The fetch records in log/pkg-fetch.jsonl at HEAD (committed, like the pin); [] when there is none."""
+    p = git("show", f"HEAD:{FETCH_REL}")
+    if p.returncode != 0:
+        return []
+    out = []
+    for line in p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").splitlines():
+        try:
+            r = json.loads(line)
+        except ValueError:
+            continue
+        if isinstance(r, dict):
+            out.append(r)
+    return out
+
+
+def pypi_path_hash(final_url, filename):
+    """The blake2b-256 hex PyPI encodes in its hashed path https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/aa/bb/<60>/<file>,
+    or None (the check tools/pkg_verify.py makes)."""
+    import urllib.parse
+    u = urllib.parse.urlparse(final_url if isinstance(final_url, str) else "")
+    if u.scheme != "https" or u.hostname != PYPI_HOST or u.query or u.fragment:
+        return None
+    parts = u.path.strip("/").split("/")
+    if len(parts) == 5 and parts[0] == "packages" and parts[4] == filename and len(parts[1]) == 2 \
+            and len(parts[2]) == 2 and len(parts[3]) == 60 and SHA_RE.match(parts[1] + parts[2] + parts[3]):
+        return parts[1] + parts[2] + parts[3]
+    return None
+
+
+def check_fetch_record(e, path, fetches):
+    """M2: a terms_guard fetch record for this url and sha256, whose PyPI path hash is the copy's blake2b-256."""
+    recs = [r for r in fetches if r.get("event") == "fetched" and r.get("via") == "terms_guard.fetch"
+            and r.get("url") == e["url"] and r.get("sha256") == e["sha256"] and r.get("file") == e["file"]]
+    if not recs:
+        raise Refused(f"{e['name']}: no terms_guard fetch record of {e['url']} with sha256 {e['sha256']} in "
+                      f"{FETCH_REL} at HEAD; fetch it with tools/pkg_fetch.py and commit the record")
+    h = hashlib.blake2b(digest_size=32)
+    with open(path, "rb") as f:
+        for block in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
+            h.update(block)
+    got = h.hexdigest()
+    if not any(pypi_path_hash(r.get("final_url"), e["file"]) == got for r in recs):
+        raise Refused(f"{e['name']}: blake2b-256 {got} of {e['file']} is not the PyPI path hash in its fetch record")
+
+
+def cache_dir():
+    return os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".cache", "pywidget", "packages")
+
+
+def verified_copy(e, dest_dir, fetches):
+    """Copy the pinned file from the cache into dest_dir, refusing a missing file, any mismatch, or a file with no
+    matching fetch record (M2)."""
+    src = os.path.join(cache_dir(), e["file"])
+    if not os.path.isfile(src) or os.path.islink(src):
+        raise Refused(f"{e['name']}: {src} is missing; fetch it through tools/terms_guard.py first")
+    dst = os.path.join(dest_dir, e["file"])
+    shutil.copyfile(src, dst)
+    got = sha256_of(dst)
+    if got != e["sha256"]:
+        raise Refused(f"{e['name']}: sha256 mismatch for {e['file']}: pinned {e['sha256']}, file {got}")
+    if "bytes" in e and os.path.getsize(dst) != e["bytes"]:
+        raise Refused(f"{e['name']}: {e['file']} is {os.path.getsize(dst)} bytes, pinned {e['bytes']}")
+    check_fetch_record(e, dst, fetches)
+    return dst
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- unpacking
+
+def unpack_wheel(path, dest):
+    """Member by member, refusing anything that could land outside dest or isn't a plain file or folder."""
+    seen = set()
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
+        for info in z.infolist():
+            n = info.filename
+            parts = n.rstrip("/").split("/")
+            if (not n or n.startswith("/") or "\\" in n or ":" in parts[0] or any(p in ("", ".", "..") for p in parts)):
+                raise Refused(f"{os.path.basename(path)}: unsafe member name {n!r}")
+            mode = (info.external_attr >> 16) & 0o170000
+            if mode not in (0, 0o100000, 0o040000):
+                raise Refused(f"{os.path.basename(path)}: member {n!r} is not a plain file (mode {oct(mode)})")
+            key = n.rstrip("/").lower()
+            if key in seen:
+                raise Refused(f"{os.path.basename(path)}: duplicate member {n!r}")
+            seen.add(key)
+        total = sum(i.file_size for i in z.infolist())
+        if total > UNPACK_CAP:
+            raise Refused(f"{os.path.basename(path)}: unpacks to {total} bytes, over the {UNPACK_CAP} cap")
+        for info in z.infolist():
+            target = os.path.join(dest, *info.filename.rstrip("/").split("/"))
+            if info.is_dir():
+                os.makedirs(target, exist_ok=True)
+                continue
+            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
+            with z.open(info) as r, open(target, "wb") as w:
+                shutil.copyfileobj(r, w)
+
+
+def unpack_sdist(path, dest):
+    """tarfile's 'data' filter refuses absolute paths, '..', links out of dest, devices; one top folder only."""
+    if not path.endswith(".tar.gz"):
+        raise Refused(f"{os.path.basename(path)} is not a .tar.gz sdist")
+    try:
+        with tarfile.open(path, "r:gz") as t:
+            tops = {m.name.split("/", 1)[0] for m in t.getmembers()}
+            if len(tops) != 1 or next(iter(tops)) in ("", ".", ".."):
+                raise Refused(f"{os.path.basename(path)}: expected one top folder, found {sorted(tops)[:5]}")
+            total = sum(m.size for m in t.getmembers())
+            if total > UNPACK_CAP:
+                raise Refused(f"{os.path.basename(path)}: unpacks to {total} bytes, over the {UNPACK_CAP} cap")
+            t.extractall(dest, filter="data")
+    except tarfile.FilterError as e:
+        raise Refused(f"{os.path.basename(path)}: unsafe member: {e}")
+    except (tarfile.TarError, EOFError, OSError) as e:
+        raise Refused(f"{os.path.basename(path)}: cannot unpack: {e}")
+    return os.path.join(dest, next(iter(tops)))
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the sandbox
+
+def sb_str(path):
+    if '"' in path or "\\" in path or "\n" in path:
+        raise Refused(f"path {path!r} cannot go into a sandbox profile")
+    return f'"{path}"'
+
+
+# Reads are deny-by-default (review B1): file contents, directory listings and xattrs are readable only under the
+# run directory, the Python install and the system paths below. Metadata (stat, readlink) stays open, because
+# path resolution needs it; it shows that a name exists, never what is in it.
+SYSTEM_READS = ["/System", "/usr/lib", "/usr/libexec", "/usr/share", "/usr/bin", "/usr/sbin", "/bin", "/sbin",
+                "/private/etc", "/dev", "[local folder]", "[local folder]", "[local folder]",
+                "/Library/Apple", "/opt/homebrew/etc/openssl@3", "/opt/homebrew/etc/ca-certificates",
+                "/opt/homebrew/share/ca-certificates"]
+# The build verb also reads the selected Xcode (cibuildwheel runs xcrun and clang).
+BUILD_READS = ["/Applications/Xcode.app", "/Library/Developer", "[local folder]",
+               "/Library/Preferences/com.apple.dt.Xcode.plist"]  # xcrun checks the licence acceptance here
+# xcrun reads its cache T/xcrun_db and may write T/xcrun_db-<suffix> temp files; the cache itself stays read-only
+# to the child, so package code cannot redirect the host's tool lookups (review L3).
+XCRUN_DB_READ = r"^[local folder][^/]+/[^/]+/T/xcrun_db(-[^/]+)?$"
+XCRUN_DB_WRITE = r"^[local folder][^/]+/[^/]+/T/xcrun_db-[^/]+$"
+# Keychain items come through these Mach services, not through files (review B2).
+KEYCHAIN_SERVICES = ["com.apple.SecurityServer", "com.apple.securityd", "com.apple.securityd.xpc", "com.apple.secd",
+                     "com.apple.security.agent", "com.apple.security.authhost", "com.apple.authd",
+                     "com.apple.security.agent.login"]
+# LaunchServices, Apple Events and launchd can each start a process outside this profile (T-0738). The Mach and
+# job-creation denies are what close that route. The three exec denies below are a backstop only, because a copy of
+# open written into the run dir is a different path.
+LAUNCH_SERVICES = ["com.apple.coreservices.launchservicesd", "com.apple.coreservices.appleevents"]
+LSD_NAMES = r"^com\.apple\.lsd\."  # a regex, so a new lsd endpoint is covered too
+NO_EXEC = ["/usr/bin/security", "/usr/bin/open", "/usr/bin/osascript", "/bin/launchctl"]
+
+
+def python_reads():
+    """The interpreter's own tree and the Homebrew kegs its dylibs come from (never site-packages: -S, -I)."""
+    out = [os.path.realpath(sys.base_prefix), os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(sys.executable))]
+    if os.path.realpath(sys.executable).startswith("/opt/homebrew/"):
+        out += ["/opt/homebrew/Cellar", "/opt/homebrew/opt"]
+    return out
+
+
+def profile(run_dir, verb="import-test"):
+    home = os.path.realpath(pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid()).pw_dir)
+    no_read = [ROOT, os.path.realpath(ROOT)] + [os.path.join(home, p) for p in (
